sources.title: JLL sells Portland carrier hotel, The Pittock Block, for $326 million

profile.research_note: Session 2026-09-03: building acquired by fifteenfortyseven (1547) Critical Systems Realty and Harrison Street Partners from JLL. Nominatim resolves the OSM coordinate to "Fork Networking" at the same street address, likely a network tenant in the carrier hotel rather than the building operator.

reading.body:
Pittock Block in Portland is a carrier hotel acquired in 2026 for $326 million by fifteenfortyseven Critical Systems Realty and Harrison Street Partners. No IT capacity or power allocation for this facility has been published by the operator. The building hosts network tenants including at least Fork Networking, but its specifications for data center load, cooling, or electrical supply are not available.

Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities and only 8 with published power capacity totaling 156.6 MW. This campus ranks ninth by published megawatts in the state, which means either its published capacity exceeds that of seven other facilities or the ranking reflects facilities that have announced expansion. Without published specifications for Pittock Block, its position in this ranking cannot be verified.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published IT specifications is the binding constraint. A carrier hotel can support GPU workloads if configured for power density and cooling, but the operator has not disclosed the capacity, power budget, or density of this facility. Until those figures are published, Pittock Block's role in AI infrastructure remains unknown.
